about: LedgerMath runs small benchmarks on real AWS machines several times a day and keeps every execution as a Run. A Series is the Runs of one benchmark, parameter set, build, instance type and Availability Zone ID; a versioned Method turns its Runs into a Derivation. This is version 1 of the data API: static JSON files cut from the Derivations and the daily price files, each kind with a JSON schema. A Series' file holds each Method's summary and its newest Runs; every Run's point is in the file of the month it started in, and months says when such a file changes.
versioning: Version 1 only ever gains fields. A field, once in a v1 file, keeps its name, its type and its meaning, and a reader ignores any field it does not know: that is why no object in the schemas index, series-list, series and series-month forbids members it does not list. A new Method, or a new version of one, is a new key beside the old ones. A change that would break a reader is published as v2, beside v1. The price files are the exception: each is the day's price file as LedgerMath keeps it, byte for byte, and follows its own schema, ledgermath.prices/1, whose root and LedgerMath's own objects are closed (AWS's objects within it are open).
figures: Every number is exactly as the Methods' Derivations hold it: nothing is rounded, and nothing is computed that the Derivations do not hold, apart from counts of a Series' Runs (in all, in a month, counted and not), the start times of its oldest and newest Run (in all, in a month), taken from its points, and each month file's sha256 and size in bytes. A duration is in nanoseconds of the Run's clock unless its field's name says otherwise; a moment is a UTC time, to the nanosecond, as the Run records it.
months: Each Series is split by month: every Run's point is in the file of the month the Run started in (UTC, by the Run's start), with series v1's entry for each pair of consecutive Runs under the month of the later Run, and the Series' file lists its months. For a given layout (the layout of v1/index.json), a month file's bytes change only when (a) a Run that started in that month is added, (b) a boot summary that was missing arrives, (c) a Run arrives late, having started before a Run of the Series already in the files, in that month or an earlier one, or (d) a Method first applies to the Series; otherwise they do not change. These four are the only causes for a given layout: layout increases when LedgerMath changes how the files are written, and only then may a file's bytes change without one of them. A past month is therefore not immutable: each entry of the Series file's months gives its month file's sha256 and size in bytes, so a reader holding a copy can tell whether it is current, and fetches the file again only when the sha256 differs. What each cause changes: (a) the month gains the Run's point, its pair entry and its count and span; (b) the point's boot_summary turns from null into the summary's address, and nothing else; (c) as (a), and in that month and every later one the points after the late Run may change only what depends on earlier Runs: their group, and requests v1's through and group_through_as_of_run (through's counts rise by exactly what the late Runs it pools add, and not at all when none of them is counted), and the pair entry of the Run right after it then comes from the late Run; (d) the Method's block appears, under its key, in every month file of the Series.

evidence.about: The evidence is served under the same address as the API: each point links its Run file (evidence), at runs/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/<id>.json, and its boot's summary (boot_summary), at boots/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/<boot>.json. A Run file names its binary, streams and dumps by hash, sha256:<hex>; each is a blob at blob_url_template with {hex} replaced by the 64 hex digits.
